arxiv-2101-11583.title: Computational strategies and estimation performance with Bayesian semiparametric Item Response Theory models
arxiv-2101-11583.creator: Sally Paganin, Christopher J. Paciorek, Claudia Wehrhahn, Abel Rodríguez, Sophia Rabe-Hesketh, Perry de Valpine
arxiv-2101-11583.description: Abstract Item response theory (IRT) models typically rely on a normality assumption for subject-specific latent traits, which is often unrealistic in practice. Semiparametric extensions based on Dirichlet process mixtures offer a more flexible representation of the unknown distribution of the latent trait.

arxiv-2110-02787.title: Relative Entropy Gradient Sampler for Unnormalized Distributions
arxiv-2110-02787.creator: Xingdong Feng, Yuan Gao, Jian Huang, Yuling Jiao, Xu Liu
arxiv-2110-02787.description: Abstract We propose a relative entropy gradient sampler (REGS) for sampling from unnormalized distributions. REGS is a particle method that seeks a sequence of simple nonlinear transforms iteratively pushing the initial samples from a reference distribution into the samples from an unnormalized target distribution.

arxiv-2202-03324.title: A Search for Technosignatures toward the Galactic Centre at 150 MHz DOI: 10.1017/pas.2026.xxx
arxiv-2202-03324.creator: Chenoa D. Tremblay 1,2, Danny C. Price 3, and Steven J. Tingay 3
arxiv-2202-03324.description: Abstract This paper is the fourth in a series of low-frequency searches for technosignatures. Using the Murchison Widefield Array over two nights we integrate 7 hours of data toward the Galactic Centre (centred on the position of Sagittarius A ∗ ) with a total field-of-view of 200 deg 2 .

arxiv-2206-09304.title: Combining acoustic bioprinting with AI-assisted Raman spectroscopy for high-throughput identification of bacteria in blood.
arxiv-2206-09304.creator: Fareeha Safir, Nhat Vu, Loza F. Tadesse, Kamyar Firouzi, Niaz Banaei, Stefanie S. Jeffrey, Amr. A. E. Saleh, Butrus (Pierre) T. Khuri-Yakub, Jennifer A. Dionne
arxiv-2206-09304.description: Abstract 2022 Abstract Identifying pathogens in complex samples such as blood, urine, and wastewater is critical to detect infection and inform optimal treatment. Surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy (SERS) and machine learning (ML) can distinguish among multiple pathogen species, but processing complex fluid samples to sensitively and specifically detect pathogens remains an outstanding challenge.

arxiv-2206-11741.title: Observation of strong backscattering in valley-Hall photonic topological interface modes
arxiv-2206-11741.creator: Christian Anker Rosiek 1,*, Guillermo Arregui 1, Anastasiia Vladimirova 1,2, Marcus Albrechtsen 1
arxiv-2206-11741.description: Abstract \defbibcheck onlynew \newrefsegment The unique properties of light underpin the visions of photonic quantum technologies, optical interconnects, and a wide range of novel sensors, but a key limiting factor today is losses due to either absorption or backscattering on defects.

arxiv-2301-04385.title: Strange and charm contributions to the HVP from C ⋆ boundary conditions
arxiv-2301-04385.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by *. collaboration We present preliminary results for the determination of the leading strange and charm quark-connected contributions to the hadronic vacuum polarization contribution to the muon’s g − 2 g-2 . Measurements are performed on the RC ⋆ collaboration’s QCD ensembles, with 3 + 1 3+1 flavors of O ⁡ ( a ) O(a) improved Wilson fermions and C ⋆ boundary conditions. The HVP is computed on a single value of the lattice spacing and two lattice volumes at unphysical pion mass.

arxiv-2309-16009.title: Floer potentials, cluster algebras and quiver representations
arxiv-2309-16009.creator: Peter Albers, Maria Bertozzi, Markus Reineke
arxiv-2309-16009.description: Abstract . We use cluster algebras to interpret Floer potentials of monotone Lagrangian tori in toric del Pezzo surfaces as cluster characters of quiver representations (see Theorem 4.3 for the precise statement). 1. Introduction In the seminal work [ 11 ] , R. Vianna constructed infinitely many pairwise non Hamiltonian isotopic monotone Lagrangian tori in the complex projective plane.

arxiv-2407-04418.title: Enabling On-Device LLMs Personalization with Smartphone Sensing DOI: 10.1145/3675094.3677545 Conference: Companion of the 2024 ACM International Joint Conference on Pervasive and Ubiquitous Computing ; October 5–9, 2024; Melbourne, VIC, Australia Companion of the 2024 ACM International Joint Confere
arxiv-2407-04418.creator: Shiquan Zhang, Ying Ma, Le Fang, Hong Jia, Simon D’Alfonso, Vassilis Kostakos
arxiv-2407-04418.description: Abstract . This demo presents a novel end-to-end framework that combines on-device large language models (LLMs) with smartphone sensing technologies to achieve context-aware and personalized services. The framework addresses critical limitations of current personalization solutions via cloud LLMs, such as privacy concerns, latency and cost, and limited personal information.

arxiv-2507-19387.title: Time-energy tradeoff in stochastic resetting using optimal control
arxiv-2507-19387.creator: Rémi Goerlich, Kristian Stølevik Olsen, Hartmut Löwen, Yael Roichman
arxiv-2507-19387.description: Abstract Stochastic resetting is a driving mechanism that is known to minimize the first passage time to reach a target, at the cost of energy expenditure. The choice of the physical implementation of each resetting event determines the tradeoff between the acceleration of the search process and its energetic cost.

arxiv-2512-18889.title: Household Plastic Recycling: Empirical Insights and Design Explorations
arxiv-2512-18889.creator: Ashley Colley, Emma Kirjavainen, Sari Tapio, Jonna Häkkilä
arxiv-2512-18889.description: Abstract . This article examines household plastic recycling in Finland through two qualitative studies and four design concepts. Study 1 reports short interviews with residents about how they store, sort, and dispose of plastic packaging in their homes. The findings highlight recurring frictions: limited space, improvised storage, uncertainty about correct sorting, and difficulties with bulky or dirty items.

arxiv-2601-03680.title: Predicting Dust Temperature from Molecular Line Data Using Machine Learning
arxiv-2601-03680.creator: Tenta Dougome, Yoshito Shimajiri, Kazuya Saigo, Sanemichi Takahashi, Miyu Kido, Shu Ishibashi, Shigehisa Takakuwa
arxiv-2601-03680.description: Abstract We conducted experiments with machine learning techniques to construct dust temperature maps from the CO isotopologue molecular line data in the Orion A molecular cloud. In the classical astrophysical methodology, multi-band continuum data are required to derive the dust temperature.

pmc-10552488.title: Linked color imaging versus white light imaging in the diagnosis of colorectal lesions: a meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials
pmc-10552488.creator: Yining Sun, Xiu-He Lv, Xian Zhang, Jin Wang, Huimin Wang, Jin-Lin Yang
pmc-10552488.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Background:Miss rate of colorectal neoplasia is associated with lesion histology, size, morphology, or location.Objectives:We aim to compare the efficacy of Linked color imaging (LCI) versus white light imaging (WLI) for adenoma detection rate (ADR), the detection of sessile serrated lesions (SSLs), serrated lesions (SLs), advanced adenomas (AAs), diminutive lesions (DLs), and flat lesions (FLs) by using per-patient and per-lesion analysis based on randomized controlled trials (RCTs).Design:Systematic review and meta-analysis.Data sources and methods:PubMed, Embase, and Cochrane databases were searched through May 1st, 2023.

pmc-10671587.title: Platelet-Rich Plasma (PRP) and Adipose-Derived Stem Cell (ADSC) Therapy in the Treatment of Genital Lichen Sclerosus: A Comprehensive Review
pmc-10671587.creator: Alessia Paganelli, Luca Contu, Alessandra Condorelli, Elena Ficarelli, Alfonso Motolese, Roberto Paganelli, Alberico Motolese
pmc-10671587.description: Lichen sclerosus (LS) is a chronic inflammatory dermatosis mostly localized in the genital area, characterized by vulvar alterations that can severely impact a patient’s quality of life. Current treatment modalities often provide incomplete relief, and there is a need for innovative approaches to manage this condition effectively.

pmc-10709068.title: In vivo evidence for GDP-fucose transport in the absence of transporter SLC35C1 and putative transporter SLC35C2
pmc-10709068.creator: Linchao Lu, Shweta Varshney, Youxi Yuan, Hua-Xing Wei, Ankit Tanwar, Subha Sundaram, Mohd Nauman, Robert S Haltiwanger, Pamela Stanley
pmc-10709068.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Slc35c1 encodes an antiporter that transports GDP-fucose into the Golgi and returns GMP to the cytoplasm. The closely related gene Slc35c2 encodes a putative GDP-fucose transporter and promotes Notch fucosylation and Notch signaling in cultured cells. Here, we show that HEK293T cells lacking SLC35C1 transferred reduced amounts of O-fucose to secreted epidermal growth factor-like repeats from NOTCH1 or secreted thrombospondin type I repeats from thrombospondin 1.

pmc-11403646.title: Lyme Neuroborreliosis in the Context of Dementia Syndromes
pmc-11403646.creator: Dzhaner H Bashchobanov, Eva Stamatova, Radina Andonova, Elena Dragusheva, Veronika Gadzhovska, Georgi Popov
pmc-11403646.description: Lyme disease (LD) can affect the skin, joints, heart, and nervous system as a multisystemic condition. The cause of the illness is the spirochete of the genus Borrelia. These pathogens can affect the skin, joints, heart, and nervous system. Lyme neuroborreliosis (LNB) is the term for the disease, which occurs when the nervous system gets involved.

pmc-11547634.title: SIMS and Numerical Analysis of Asymmetrical Out-Diffusion of Hydrogen and Carbon in CdxZn1−xO:Eu Multilayer
pmc-11547634.creator: Zeinab Khosravizadeh, Anastasiia Lysak, Ewa Przeździecka, Rafał Jakieła
pmc-11547634.description: This study employs secondary ion mass spectrometry (SIMS) to investigate the diffusion behavior of hydrogen and carbon in a CdxZn1−xO:Eu multilayer at different annealing temperatures (500–900 °C). The SIMS results reveal a significant out-diffusion of these elements toward the surface and diffusion to the interface region. The diffusion flow rates are asymmetric and favor the interface direction.

pmc-11712740.title: Impact of Yoga in Transformation of Quality of Life of Alzheimer’s disease cases
pmc-11712740.creator: Meenakshi Kaushik
pmc-11712740.description: BackgroundAlzheimer’s disease (AD) constitutes a formidable challenge, profoundly affecting the fabric of individuals' lives and intricately entwined with disturbances in their quality of life. This study embarks on a mission to unravel the transformative potential of a carefully crafted 12‐week yoga intervention, specifically tailored to address the multifaceted dimensions of quality of life.

pmc-11735664.title: Acid–base and electrolyte changes in dogs after packed red blood cell transfusion
pmc-11735664.creator: P Bou, I Mesa, R F Ferreira, C Torrente, E G Manzanilla, L Bosch
pmc-11735664.description: BackgroundPacked RBC (pRBC) transfusions are often necessary to enhance organ perfusion and tissue oxygenation in cases of severe anemia.ObjectivesWe aimed to describe changes in acid–base and biochemical parameters in dogs after transfusion of pRBC and potential effects on the outcome.MethodsThe prospective observational study included anemic dogs requiring pRBC transfusions.

pmc-11862676.title: “Esketamine” in Borderline Personality Disorder: focud on suicide ideation
pmc-11862676.creator: M. Olivola, F. Mazzoni, V. Arienti, S. C. Civardi, G. Carnevale Miacca, P. Leali, F. Santilli, A. Guffanti, N. Brondino
pmc-11862676.description: IntroductionBorderline personality disorder is often associated with comorbid conditions such as eating disorders, mood disorders, and substance use disorders. The prevalence of BPD and major depressive disorder (MDD) are about 5.9% and 8%, respectively, but up to 80% of patients with BPD experience one or more episodes of MDD in their lifetime.

pmc-12638469.title: Improvement in the quality of the water-saving and drought-resistant rice ‘Huhan 1516’ via molecular markers
pmc-12638469.creator: Yanan Wang, Ao Li, Anning Zhang, Deyan Kong, E Li, Lei Wang, Yi Liu, Xingxing Luo, Mengchen Li, Lijun Luo, Feiming Wang
pmc-12638469.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). To improve the rice quality of the water-saving and drought-resistant rice variety ‘Huhan 1516’ and cultivate high-yield, high-quality new lines of water-saving and drought-resistant rice. In this study, we used ‘Meixiangzhan 2’, which carries the flavour gene Badh2, as the donor parent and ‘Huhan 1516’, which contains the rice blast resistance gene Pi2, as the recipient parent and comprehensively utilized molecular marker-assisted selection (MAS) and the WDR 6K microarray detection system for selection.

pmc-12928454.title: A mixed methods evaluation of a pilot open trial of a mentor-guided digital intervention for youth anxiety
pmc-12928454.creator: Emma C. Wolfe, Alexandra Werntz, Audrey Michel, Yiyang Zhang, Mark Rucker, Mehdi Boukhechba, Laura E. Barnes, Jean E. Rhodes, Bethany A. Teachman, Haleh Ayatollahi, Haleh Ayatollahi, Haleh Ayatollahi, Haleh Ayatollahi
pmc-12928454.description: Digital mental health interventions (DMHIs), such as cognitive bias modification for interpretations (CBM-I), offer promise for increasing access to anxiety treatment among underserved adolescents, but data regarding their efficacy are mixed. Paraprofessionals and other caring adults in youth’s lives, such as non-parental adult mentors, may be able to support the use of DMHIs and increase teen engagement.

pmc-13096116.title: Prevalence of Bacillus species in the lytic cultural heritage of Santa Lucia alle Malve Rupestrian Church
pmc-13096116.creator: Matteo Santacroce, Jakub Baranek, Zbigniew Adamski, Artur Trzebny, Miroslawa Dabert, Sabino A. Bufo, Laura Scrano
pmc-13096116.description: Santa Lucia alle Malve (SLM) is a unique rupestrian heritage site, entirely carved into limestone. This monument, which was a church in the ancient settlement of Benedictine nuns over a millennium ago in southern Italy, holds exceptional value not only from an architectural and cultural perspective but also in terms of its microbial ecology.

pmc-13305900.title: P23 A survey of physician practice, knowledge and attitudes towards penicillin allergy labels and penicillin desensitization in the intensive care unit
pmc-13305900.creator: John E A Taylor, Neil Powell, Andrew F Whyte, Rob Jackson, Jennie Stephens, Jonathan Sandoe
pmc-13305900.description: BackgroundPenicillin allergy labels are reported in approximately 10% of patients, yet over 90% of these labels are inaccurate when formally tested. This mislabelling has important implications for antimicrobial stewardship, as it leads to avoidance of first-line β-lactam antibiotics, resulting in the unnecessary use of broad-spectrum alternatives, increased risk of resistant infections, and higher healthcare costs.
